intro: WELCOME. This is a realistic-opponent repertoire for White built around the King's Indian Attack (KIA) — a universal system rather than a single opening, where White reaches essentially the same structure (pawns on d3/e4, knights on d2/f3, a fianchettoed bishop on g2, and castled kingside) regardless of whether Black plays the French, the Sicilian, the Caro-Kann, or almost anything else. Built the same way as the companion Sicilian, Queen's Gambit, Indian Defenses, and English Opening encyclopedias: main plans, common tries you'll actually meet, sharp lines, typical mistakes, every line verified move-by-move for legality. PLANNED TABLE OF CONTENTS — Chapter 1: Understanding the King's Indian Attack (foundations — the universal setup, the e4-e5 bind, when it works and when it doesn't). Chapter 2: The KIA vs. the French Defense. Chapter 3: The KIA vs. the Sicilian Defense. Chapter 4: The KIA vs. the Caro-Kann Defense. Chapter 5: The KIA vs. 1...e5 and Other Setups Without a Bind. Chapter 6: The 1.Nf3 Move Order (the Barcza System) and Black's Independent Tries. Chapter 7: The Kingside Attack in Depth. Chapter 8: Traps and Tactics Compendium. Chapters will be built and appended one at a time, with every line verified for legality and spot-checked against current theory before being added.
